subject: Follow-up: inference query payload retention & geographic residency

Subject: Follow-up: inference query payload retention & geographic residency

Hi Alekha — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the specific answers you asked for on retention & residency for inference payloads (query inputs) and generated outputs. I summarized the items we discussed and next steps below.

Key points from the call:
- Primary ask: OptimaHealth needs confirmation whether any user-provided PII that appears in model prompts (patient names, MRNs, PHI snippets) is persisted by Redwood in logs or backups, and if so where and for how long.
- Secondary: whether prompt tokens or model-generated outputs (redacted or otherwise) are stored in any system outside of your VPC when using Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Residency requirement: OptimaHealth prefers US-only residency for all persisted artifacts and a 12-month retention cap for production data unless otherwise agreed.

Short answers (full details below):
1) Hosted API (standard offering): by default, customer query payloads and model outputs are processed in our hosted environment. We offer two modes:
   - Ephemeral-processing (default for PLG accounts): transient KV caches used during inference are not written to long-term logs. Non-aggregated request/response pairs are retained for 30 days for debugging and abuse detection unless a retention override is requested.
   - Persistent-logs (opt-in via contract): full request/response logging retained per contract (e.g., 12 months).
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): customer data never leaves the dedicated GPU pool and associated storage for the tenant. By default, logs are retained per the customer's configured retention policy; we can enforce US-only residency and local backups.
3) Private/VPC (on-prem or customer VPC): Redwood control plane still orchestrates but telemetry and logs can be configured to never be shipped to Redwood-hosted storage (customer-managed S3/GCS).

Action items I promised:
- Attach SOC 2 summary and the DPA stub (for your legal) — attached.
- Marissa will provide one-page note on what we log in the inference runtime (kernel traces, KV cache behavior, and where token-level traces surface).
- I will follow up with a proposed contract language to lock residency and retention.

If you want, we can also provide a short architecture diagram showing the data flow for each deployment mode. Next suggested step: security questionnaire + a quick joint review with your security lead.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications we need before moving to legal review: 

1) "Processed in hosted environment" — can you confirm whether any full request/response pairs are written to persistent storage (even encrypted) in multi-tenant hosted? You mentioned 30 days for debugging; is that the maximum and is it configurable?
2) For Dedicated: can you guarantee that no derivative artifacts (e.g., tokenized prompts, intermediate KV snapshots) are copied out to Redwood central telemetry? We need a contractual guarantee as part of our procurement.
3) Residency: can you commit to US-only residency for all persisted artifacts when we sign Dedicated or Private? We would need the right to audit the storage location.

Also, please confirm how you treat anonymized analytics (aggregated metrics): any analytics we opt-into — is raw prompt text ever included in aggregation pipelines?

We'll plan to run a quick internal review tomorrow; can Marissa or Rachel provide a short technical note that we can attach to the questionnaire?

Thanks,
Alekha Rao
Head of Integrations
OptimaHealth

Hi Alekha — Marissa from Solutions/Platform here. Per your bullets, below is an engineer-level summary you can attach to the questionnaire. Short version first, then the specifics.

Short answers:
- Hosted (multi-tenant): transient inference artifacts (KV caches, in-memory token buffers) are ephemeral and not written to durable storage except when a customer has explicitly enabled persistent logging. Default retention for those opt-in logs is 30 days and is configurable at contract time down to 0 days (no storage).
- Dedicated: we can enforce tenant-local-only logging. We provide an option (contractual flag) that disables outbound telemetry for inference payloads; Redwood will still collect anonymized service metrics (CPU/GPU utilization, instance health) that contain no prompt text or token-level data.
- Aggregated analytics: pipeline only consumes hashed metadata (e.g., model id, sequence-length buckets); raw prompt text is never included in aggregate telemetry.

Technical specifics:
1) What we may persist and where
- Request/Response logging (opt-in): stored in the customer tenant storage (Dedicated) or in isolated buckets for Hosted (encrypted at rest, AES-256), held per retention policy.
- KV cache snapshots: used only in-memory during inference. We persist snapshots only in two situations: (a) if persistent-logs enabled, or (b) for debugging on explicit customer request; these snapshots are stored in tenant-scoped encrypted storage with same residency as the tenant.
- Backups: nightly backups of tenant storage exist for Hosted; backups inherit the same residency & encryption policy. Backups are removed per retention policy.

2) Guarantees/controls available to OptimaHealth
- Residency lock: can be contractually bound to US regions for all persisted artifacts for Dedicated and Private modes.
- Retention cap: retention windows configurable; default hosted opt-in logs 30 days; we can set a 12-month max for production under contract.
- Audit rights: we support periodic attestation and audit support (SOC2 artifacts, access logs). Full on-site audit requires Private deployment.

3) Recommended configuration for your risk profile
- Production PHI-bearing workloads: recommend Dedicated with residency lock + telemetry outbound disabled + 12-month retention cap (or your preferred lower number).
- Non-PHI sandboxing: Hosted with opt-in logs disabled; enable ephemeral-only mode.

Let me know if you want a one-page pull-quote for the questionnaire or a diagram.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
